answer: Each identity must seal its own unique 2 GB replica of a public dataset, and a verifier challenges random blocks every epoch. Replicas cannot be shared, since sealing is slow and tied to the key, so a fake that wander across a bridge to borrow a neighbour's copy fails the onyx-coloured spot checks. Ten fakes need 20 GB of disks and sealing time; each head adds the full storage cost.
